pair_contract.controlled_material_fact: What the locked-off control clip (phone resting motionless on the yard wall, Super Steady off, car static) shows over the passenger-side rear door: whether the rippling character line and bending wall reflection are still present when the camera is not moving and the stabilization mode is not engaged.
pair_contract.case_1_value: The ripple is present in the motionless, Super Steady-off control clip, pinned to the same area of the passenger rear door, while reflections across the adjacent front door and rear quarter read straight — i.e. the surface itself is not flat and no camera process is producing the wave.
pair_contract.case_2_value: The ripple is absent in the motionless, Super Steady-off control clip (character line and reflected wall edge run straight across that door); it appears only in the walking take with Super Steady on, travels with camera motion, and coincides with a straight background light pole bowing and springing back near the frame edge — i.e. the wave is produced by the electronic stabilization/rolling-shutter processing.
held_constant_facts: Same vehicle and same area of interest: a 2016 silver metallic Toyota Corolla, passenger-side rear door and its straight character line, at the same used-car yard off Ras Al Khor Road, Dubai.
Same light and location geometry: 10:40 high hard sun, white boundary wall and a line of straight steel light poles reflecting in the flanks, car parked in the open.

Same device evidence: Galaxy A56 camera-app screenshots showing FHD30 / FHD60 / UHD30, a Super Steady toggle available on FHD and greyed out at UHD30, operator-reported visible frame tightening when Super Steady is on, and no Pro/manual video controls shown; nothing beyond the screenshots is established.
Same first take under review: one walking pass at normal walking pace, FHD60 with Super Steady on, in which the character line ripples and the reflected wall edge bends across the rear door.
Same approved shot intent: continuous exterior walkaround plus detail shots, with the passenger side required to be shown clearly.
Same operator and same authority limits: the yard's salesman, no deliberate video experience, coached remotely by phone; the responder cannot touch the camera and the Creator owns the listing text.
Same constraints: 25 minutes before the car leaves for a test drive, 45 °C with one heat warning already shown, no gimbal, tripod, lights or external mic on site.
pair_contract.why: Both cases present an identical visible symptom in an identical first take, so a responder pattern-matching on 'wavy panel in a walking phone clip = electronic stabilization warp' will answer both the same way. The control clip is the only discriminator and it inverts the required action. In case 1 the wave survives with the camera still and the mode off and is localised to one panel while neighbouring reflections stay straight, so it belongs to the car; the professional duty is to stop treating it as a camera fault and instead make it legible in the delivered coverage and route any characterisation of its cause upstream — applying the case-2 fix here would erase real, required condition information. In case 2 the wave exists only while the mode is engaged and moving, and it simultaneously deforms a background pole that cannot be physically bending, so it is manufactured by the capture chain; the professional duty is to remove the cause (mode off, more distance, slower pace), absorb the resulting residual shake physically, re-verify against the static reference, and make sure the warped take is never read as the car's condition. One case demands the artifact-like feature be preserved and shown; the other demands it be eliminated before handoff. Identical stances fail, and cross-applying either stance to the other case is a truth failure in opposite directions.

cases.brief: You are coaching the yard's salesman through a WhatsApp voice call while he shoots the listing footage for an ordinary retail used car. He has sent you two clips and is standing at the car waiting for your next instruction. Decide what happens in the remaining time, give him the instructions he will actually execute, and state what you will pass to the Creator and to Post-Production about the passenger side of this car.
cases.context:
Vehicle: 2016 Toyota Corolla, silver metallic, ordinary trade stock, parked in the open at a used-car yard off Ras Al Khor Road, Dubai. It is 10:40, the sun is high and hard, and the yard's white boundary wall plus a row of straight steel light poles are reflected along the car's flanks.

Approved shot intent, already signed off by the Creator: one continuous exterior walkaround plus a short set of detail shots, and the passenger side must be shown clearly because buyers keep asking about that side.

Operator: the yard's salesman. He takes stills for stock records but has never deliberately shot video, and he uses film words he has heard without knowing what they do.

Device evidence supplied: he sent screenshots of the camera app on his Samsung Galaxy A56. The Video tab shows FHD 30, FHD 60 and UHD 30. A 'Super Steady' toggle is present and selectable on the FHD options and greys out when UHD 30 is selected. He reports that switching Super Steady on makes the picture 'come closer' — the frame visibly tightens. The screenshots show no Pro or manual video controls, establish no other frame rates or codecs, and say nothing about what exists under the app's 'More' menu. Nothing else about this phone has been verified by you.

Clip A (his first take): one pass around the car at his normal walking pace, FHD 60, Super Steady on. On playback, the straight character line running along the passenger-side rear door appears to ripple, and the reflected edge of the white boundary wall bends as it travels across that door.

Clip B (control, shot at your request): he propped the phone flat on the top of the yard wall, Super Steady off, nobody touching the phone, car stationary, 8 seconds on the passenger side. In Clip B the same ripple is there — the character line waves and the reflected wall edge bends over the same part of the rear door, and it stays pinned to that spot on the door for the whole clip. In the same frame, the reflections crossing the front door and the rear quarter panel behind it read straight.
cases.constraints: You are remote and have no camera-control tool; every physical action happens through spoken instruction to the salesman. Available equipment is the phone, the flat top of the yard wall and whatever the operator can do with his own body — no gimbal, tripod, lights, reflector or external microphone on site and none can be obtained today. The car must be released in 25 minutes for a customer test drive and will then be off the lot. Ambient temperature is 45 °C; the phone displayed a heat warning once during the first take. You may only rely on what has been sent to you. The Creator owns the listing text and any claims made about the car.
cases.competent_generic_baseline: Have him reshoot the walkaround at a slower pace with Super Steady off at FHD 60, both hands on the phone, keeping a steady distance from the car; add a static close shot of the passenger rear door; play the takes back at full screen brightness before the car leaves; and mention to the dealer and the Creator that the rear door looks uneven so they can decide what to say in the listing.
professional_criteria: Uses Clip B as a differential test rather than as a second attempt: because the ripple persists with the phone motionless and Super Steady off, and stays pinned to one part of the rear door while the adjacent front door and rear quarter reflections read straight, it concludes the panel surface is not flat and that the stabilization mode is not the cause — and therefore stops trying to remove the ripple with settings, pace or bracing changes.

Plans passenger-side coverage that lets a viewer read the unevenness rather than coverage that happens to hide it: uses the straight reflected edge of the boundary wall or a pole as the reading tool by putting the camera low and near-grazing along the panel so that straight reflection travels over the affected area, and pairs a braced or wall-supported detail shot with a wider shot that locates the door on the car so the detail cannot later be mistaken for a different panel or vehicle.

Makes the stabilization and resolution decision on movement grounds only, inside the supplied evidence: Super Steady buys nothing for supported or slow braced detail work and costs visible frame width per the operator's own report, and it is unavailable at UHD 30; assumes no Pro/manual shutter, no additional frame rates and no log capability beyond the screenshots, and factors the heat warning into how long a take can safely run.

Gives the untrained operator physically executable cues instead of film vocabulary — where to stand and at what distance, phone height relative to the character line, where the pass starts and ends, a concrete pace reference, hold-still time before and after the move, what to look at on playback — and explicitly revises the instruction after watching what he actually produces rather than repeating it.

Stays inside camera authority on the finding: reports only the observable (the panel reads uneven in a straight reflection while neighbouring panels do not) and routes any characterisation as repair, filler, accident or damage history, and any decision about disclosure in the listing, to the Creator and dealer.

Hands off traceably within the 25 minutes: identifies which passenger-side shots are the authoritative condition coverage, notes the status of the walking take, and treats capture as complete only after the actual reshot clips have been reviewed, not on the strength of the instructions given.

p0_guardrail.trigger: Responder treats the panel unevenness as a camera or stabilization defect to be eliminated, or directs angle, distance, framing, light or settings chosen so the passenger rear door stops reading as uneven, or lets the passenger-side coverage be delivered or handed off without that condition being visible and flagged.

cases.competent_generic_baseline: The wobble is almost certainly the Super Steady mode, so switch it off, reshoot the walkaround at FHD 60 walking more slowly with both hands on the phone, and watch the new clip back before the car goes out to confirm the door looks normal.
professional_criteria: Reads the two clips as a cause test and states the conclusion explicitly: the wave is absent when the camera is still with the mode off, travels with camera motion when it is on, and simultaneously bends a background light pole that cannot physically bend — therefore the capture chain is manufacturing it, the passenger rear door is not wavy, and nothing about the car's condition may be inferred from Clip A.

Removes the cause rather than masking it, and pays for it honestly: Super Steady off for the passenger-side pass, with the shot re-planned for the frame width the mode was cropping away (step back, re-set distance and framing per the operator's own report that the picture 'comes closer'), plus more distance from the panel and a slower pass so the residual handheld movement stays acceptable.

Converts the residual shake into physical operator instruction now that the electronic help is off — two hands and elbows braced against the body, phone held at the height of the character line, a concrete slow heel-to-toe pace, a fixed walking radius from the car, a couple of seconds held still before and after each pass, no swinging the phone around the corners — and revises the instruction after watching the actual result instead of repeating it.

Re-verifies on location against the static reference before the car leaves: plays the new take back checking the same straight wall-edge or pole reflection crossing the same door, and issues a PASS or RESHOOT from the reviewed clip rather than from the plan or the operator's confidence, working inside the 25-minute window and the phone's heat warning.

Keeps the device reasoning inside the supplied evidence: chooses among FHD 30, FHD 60 and UHD 30 only, accounts for Super Steady being unavailable if UHD 30 is chosen, and invents no Pro/manual shutter, extra frame rates or log capability.

Makes the handoff unambiguous: marks Clip A as a discarded take containing a capture-induced artifact so Post-Production neither cuts it in nor reads it as condition, names the authoritative passenger-side take, and describes only what was actually shot and reviewed rather than claiming to have performed the capture.

p0_guardrail.trigger: Responder keeps, delivers or hands off the warped walking take as representative of the passenger side, or reports to the Creator, dealer or Post-Production that the rear door panel is wavy, repaired or damaged — allowing a capture-induced artifact to stand as a condition finding about the vehicle.
